items.followUp: Differentiate between an atom and an ion.

rubric.why: This states the defining feature of an atom.
rubric.description: Defines an atom as the smallest particle of an element that takes part in a chemical reaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the atom as the smallest particle of an element involved in a chemical reaction.

rubric.why: This distinguishes a molecule from an atom by its independent existence and retained properties.
rubric.description: Defines a molecule as the smallest particle of a substance that can exist independently and retain its properties.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a molecule as an independently existing particle that retains the substance's properties.

modelAnswer: An atom is the smallest particle of an element that takes part in a chemical reaction.
A molecule is the smallest particle of a substance that can exist independently and retain its properties.

items.followUp: Write the electronic configuration of an oxide ion, O²⁻.

rubric.why: A chlorine atom gains one electron to form Cl⁻, giving it 18 electrons.
rubric.description: Identifies the total number of electrons in Cl⁻ as 18.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that Cl⁻ has 18 electrons.

rubric.why: The 18 electrons occupy the shells in the configuration 2, 8, 8.
rubric.description: Gives the correct shell electronic configuration.

modelAnswer: A chlorine atom has 17 electrons; Cl⁻ gains one electron, so it has 18 electrons.

items.followUp: Complete the nuclear equation: ___ + ___ → ¹⁴₆C + ¹₁H.

rubric.why: The reactants are the boron-11 nucleus and a deuterium nucleus.
rubric.description: Identifies the reactant nuclei as ¹¹₅B and ²₁H.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for writing the correct reactant isotopes.

rubric.why: The nuclear equation conserves both mass number and atomic number.
rubric.description: Balances the equation to give ¹¹₅B + ²₁H → ¹²₆C + ¹₀n.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correctly balanced equation.

items.followUp: How are elements arranged in groups in the periodic table?

rubric.why: A period is a horizontal row in the periodic table.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that periods are horizontal rows.

rubric.why: Elements in a period are listed by increasing atomic number and have the same number of occupied shells.
rubric.description: States the arrangement by increasing atomic number and/or the shared shell count of elements in a period.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that atomic number increases across a period, or that elements in the same period have the same number of electron shells.

modelAnswer: Elements are arranged in horizontal rows called periods.
Across a period, atomic number increases; elements in the same period have the same number of occupied electron shells.

rubric.why: Periodicity means that similar properties recur at intervals.
rubric.description: States that the properties of elements repeat periodically.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that element properties repeat or recur periodically.

rubric.why: The periodic repetition occurs when elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number.
rubric.description: Relates the periodic repetition of properties to increasing atomic number.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying increasing atomic number as the basis for the periodic repetition.

modelAnswer: A periodic function is a property that repeats at regular intervals.
When elements are arranged in order of increasing atomic number, their properties repeat periodically.

items.followUp: Define electron affinity and state a commonly used unit for it.

rubric.why: This gives the defining process for first ionization energy.
rubric.description: Defines ionization energy as the energy needed to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition, including removal of an electron from a gaseous atom.

rubric.why: Ionization energy is commonly expressed per mole of atoms.
rubric.description: Gives the unit as kJ mol⁻¹.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the unit kJ mol⁻¹.

modelAnswer: Ionization energy is the energy required to remove an electron from an isolated gaseous atom.

items.followUp: What is meant by the octet rule?

rubric.why: The duplet rule refers to a stable outer shell containing two electrons.
rubric.description: States that an atom becomes stable when its outermost shell has two electrons.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying two electrons in the outermost shell as the duplet.

rubric.why: The duplet represents the stable arrangement of helium's first shell.
rubric.description: Connects the duplet arrangement with the stable configuration of helium.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that atoms attain the stable, helium-like arrangement.

modelAnswer: According to the duplet rule, an atom becomes stable when its outermost shell contains two electrons.
This is the stable electronic arrangement of helium.

items.followUp: What is meant by a polar covalent bond?

rubric.why: Equal sharing of the bonding electron pair is the key feature of a non-polar covalent bond.
rubric.description: States that the bonding electrons are shared equally between the bonded atoms.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the electron pair is shared equally.

rubric.why: Equal sharing means there is no charge separation across the bond.
rubric.description: Identifies the absence of bond polarity, commonly because the atoms are identical or have similar electronegativity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that there are no poles/partial charges, or that the bond is between atoms with similar electronegativity.

modelAnswer: A non-polar covalent bond is formed when the bonded atoms share the bonding electron pair equally.
There is no separation of charge across the bond; it commonly forms between identical atoms or atoms with similar electronegativity.
